theater: 殷與奄（豫北安陽至魯南曲阜）

battle.name: 三監之亂
battle.theater: 殷與奄（豫北安陽至魯南曲阜）
battle.brief: 公元前1042年，武王崩而成王幼弱，周公旦攝政；其弟管叔、蔡叔、霍叔挾武庚與殷民叛於殷畿，奄國自東來援。周公領王師東征，前後約三年，先誅武庚於殷，再滅奄於魯南，戰線自安陽推至曲阜。卡面埃及月牙劍未隨軍而至，但商周雙方的近身砍殺同屬青銅時代早期弧刃格殺一脉，中原陣上用的是青銅戈、鉞與矛。

kit.name: 埃及月牙劍
kit.history: 外彎的單刃劍，砍下去不用拔。它比直劍更早出現在埃及人的手上。

countries: 三監之亂爆發於公元前1042年商周鼎革之際，交戰的兩方一邊是周王室及其分封諸侯，另一邊是商朝遺緒與東方方國組成的聯盟。叛方以商王帝辛之子武庚為旗幟，名義上重立殷祀；主導者是周武王的三子管叔鮮、蔡叔度與霍叔（三人名諱各書不一），這三人正是周公旦的同母兄弟，武王在世時分封於管、蔡、霍三地，周人稱之為「三監」——「監」是治理、監臨的意思，並非監獄。叛方還得到東方大國奄的支持；奄是商代東方的方國，商亡之後始終未被周人有效控制，國都在今山東曲阜、萊蕪一帶。奄的加入，使這場叛亂由畿內的反叛升級為東西兩線並進的戰爭。正方是周公旦攝政的周王廷：成王姬誦年幼，軍國大政由周公一人代掌，兵源以王師、殷畿新附之地以及周原、關中的老本為主；齊、魯、衛、燕、宋等受封諸侯承擔守土的任務，是東征之後才出現的事。雙方的指揮系統都極簡：叛方靠血緣與對商遺民的號召，沒有固定編制與統一軍令；周方則有周公一人統攝兵、糧、刑與祭祀，並把軍事行動寫進誓師與告文之中，納入禮制的框架。這是一場開國者自己家族內部的分裂，也是新秩序能否站住的第一次實戰考驗。
countriesEn: The Sanmon rising broke out in 1042 BC, at the moment when the Zhou were taking over from the Shang. On one side stood the Zhou royal house together with the lords it enfeoffed; on the other stood a coalition formed by the surviving Shang house and by the subject polities of the east. The rebels carried the banner of Wu Geng, son of the last Shang king Di Xin, and pretended in his name to re-establish the sacrifice to the Shang. Those who drove the rising were the three sons of King Wu: Guan Shu Xian, Cai Shu Du and Huo Shu, whose personal names differ from book to book. They were brothers of the Duke of Zhou by the same mother, and King Wu had enfeoffed them at Guan, Cai and Huo; the Zhou called them the Three Supervisors, and the word means those who govern and supervise, not jailers. The rebels also drew in the support of the eastern state of Yan, a great Shang-era polity that the Zhou had never brought properly under control and whose capital lay around Qufu and Laiwu in what is now Shandong. The entry of Yan turned what might have been a rising in the royal heartland into a war fought on two fronts, east and west. On the other side was the court of the Zhou under the regency of the Duke of Zhou, Dan: King Cheng, Ji Song, was a child, and the Duke held the army, the finances, the penal law and the sacrifices on his own authority. The strength at his disposal was the royal host, the newly submitted districts of the Yin region and the old base of the Zhou in the Guanzhong basin; the great lords of Qi, Lu, Wei, Yan and Song only came into existence as holders of land after the campaign. Both command structures were rudimentary. The rebels relied on blood ties and on their ability to call up the Shang remnant, with no permanent establishment and no standing orders. The Zhou side had one man, the Duke of Zhou, coordinating troops, grain, punishments and ritual, and the proclamations preserved in the chapters of the Shujing brought the war inside the frame of ritual. This was a split inside the family of the founder of the dynasty, and it was the first field test of whether the new order could stand.
people: 捲入這場叛亂的人，幾乎全是周王室的至親。周公旦是全場主角：武王崩後，他以周公的名義攝政，面對兄弟的流言與武庚的叛軍，他先以《多士》《多方》諸篇所存的告誥之辭安撫人心，再舉兵東征；傳世記載稱他「居東二年，則罪人斯得」，平亂之後營建洛邑、還政於成王，傳為周公製禮作樂的由來。成王姬誦是武王之子，戰時年幼；據《召誥》所記，他曾到豐、至洛陽，親自參與營邑的籌劃，後來成了王室正統性的象徵。叛方領袖是三兄弟：管叔鮮居管、蔡叔度居蔡、霍叔居霍，都是周王的兒子、周公的弟弟；他們散布「周公將不利於孺子」的流言，又鼓動封地內的商遺民起兵。商王血脈方面，武庚以帝辛之子的身分居殷，被視為殷祀的正統繼承人，兵敗後被誅。站在周公一邊的還有康叔度與召公奭：康叔度參與平亂，事後封於衛；召公奭佐成王營洛邑，後封於燕，是西周封建的柱石。傳世文獻還留下一位少年的名字：成王弟姬利相傳曾在周公攝政時與人商議請周公讓位，雖是後世附會，卻說明當時的權力交接並非毫無爭議。西周一代的史官則把這段記憶寫成了天命與德行的樣板，後世儒家援引「周公攝政」「還政於成王」，把它說成一次可以放手的統治。
peopleEn: The people caught up in this rising were, almost without exception, the closest kin of the Zhou royal house. The Duke of Zhou, Dan, was the central figure of the whole affair: after King Wu died he took charge as regent under the title of the Duke of Zhou, and faced with the slander of his brothers and the army of Wu Geng he first calmed hearts with the proclamations preserved in the chapters of the Shujing, the Duo Shi and the Duo Fang, and only then marched east. The received account has it that he stayed in the east two years, and then the guilty were taken, and after the rising was put down he built the city of Luoyang and returned the government to King Cheng; this became the origin of the story that the Duke of Zhou made the rites and the music. King Cheng, Ji Song, was the son of King Wu and was a child at the time. The chapter Zao Gao has it that he came to Feng and went on to Luoyang and took part himself in the planning of the new city, and he later became the very image of legitimate kingship. The leaders of the rebels were three brothers: Guan Shu Xian at Guan, Cai Shu Du at Cai and Huo Shu at Huo, all sons of King Wu and younger brothers of the Duke of Zhou. They spread the rumour that the Duke of Zhou meant harm to the child prince, and they stirred the Shang remnant within their own fiefs to take up arms. On the side of the Shang bloodline, Wu Geng, the son of Di Xin, held Yin as the legitimate successor of the Shang sacrifice, and was executed after his defeat. On the Duke's side stood Kang Shu Du and Shao Gong Shi: Kang Shu Du took part in putting down the rising and was afterwards enfeoffed in Wei, while Shao Gong Shi assisted King Cheng in laying out the city at Luoyang and was later enfeoffed in Yan, a pillar of the Zhou feudal order. The transmitted texts preserve the name of one boy as well: the younger brother of King Cheng, Ji Li, is said to have joined with others in discussing the idea of asking the Duke to give way. Later embellishment though it is, it shows that the transfer of authority at that moment was not free of dispute. The historiographers of the early Western Zhou turned the memory into a model of the Mandate of Heaven and of moral virtue, and later Confucians cited the regency of the Duke of Zhou and his return of power to King Cheng as a case of rule that knew how to let go.
kits: 卡面這把埃及月牙劍（khopesh）並沒有出現在周人的軍陣之中。它是埃及自早王朝以來就用於近身格殺的青銅弧刃單刃劍：刃口開在凸面，砍進人體或盾牌之後不必回抽，比直刃劍更早成熟，約在公元前1550年前後的埃及新王國時期，逐漸讓位給直背劍與更長的青銅刃器。把它放進三監之亂的裝備表，是因為它代表青銅時代早期「弧刃格殺」這一條技術路線，而商周陣上真正用來砍殺的兵器，正是同一條路線在中原的另一個分支：青銅戈。戈是裝在木柲上的斧刃刀，援部出鋒、內部帶銦，作戰動作以鉤啄與斫擊為主，與月牙劍「砍下去不用拔」的邏輯同源，只是柄長、槓桿更長。與戈並列的是青銅矛，箭鏃形的矛頭安在木柲上；還有青銅鉞，鉞是斧形，既是兵器，也是統軍、賞罰的象徵。遠射靠弓，以木、骨、石為鏃；防護止於木牌與皮革，西周中期的金屬甲胄尚未普及。機動靠雙輪單軸的車，一車通常乘三人，御者居中，右手持矛，左手持戈或弓；車是軍隊的骨架，步兵是數量。攻城方面沒有投石機與衝車，周人靠圍城、斷糧與版築築城，凸顯出洛陽成周遺址的夯土牆基。運輸靠牛車與人力，軍糧一部分就地向殷地徵發，一部分由周原後方輸送。
kitsEn: The Egyptian khopesh on the card did not appear in the Zhou army. It was a bronze single-edged sword of crescent curvature used in Egypt for close combat from the Old Kingdom onward: the edge was on the convex side, and once it had been driven into a body or a shield it did not have to be pulled back out, so it matured earlier than the straight-edged sword, and around 1550 BC, in the New Kingdom, it was gradually displaced by straight-backed swords and by longer bronze blades. It belongs in the equipment table of the Sanmon rising because it represents the early Bronze Age line of technique of the arc-bladed hack, and the weapons actually used to cut and slash on the Shang and Zhou fields were precisely a branch of that same line in the Central Plain: the bronze ge. A ge is an axe-shaped blade fitted to a wooden shaft, with a pointed upper blade and a socketed tang, worked mainly by hooking, pulling and chopping, which follows the same logic as the khopesh that one does not withdraw after striking, only with a longer haft and a longer lever. Alongside the ge stood the bronze spear, its arrowhead-shaped head mounted on a wooden shaft, and the bronze yue, an axe-form weapon that was at once a weapon and an emblem of command, of reward and of punishment. Missiles were shot with the bow, using points of wood, bone and stone; protection stopped at wooden shields and leather, for metal harness was not yet general in the middle Western Zhou. Mobility came with the chariot, two wheels on one axle, usually carrying three men, the driver in the middle with a spear in his right hand and a ge or bow in his left; the chariot was the skeleton of the army and the foot its numbers. There were no stone-throwers and no battering rams: the Zhou invested cities, cut their grain and built walls by ramming earth between boards, as the rammed-earth wall bases of the completed Zhou at Luoyang still show. Transport was by ox cart and human porter, and the grain of the army was drawn partly from the Yin country on the spot and partly carried from the Zhou plain behind.
tactics: 周公應對這場叛亂，先走的是政治與後勤，再走的是戰場。史存《尚書·大誥》《康誥》《酒誥》《梓材》《多士》《多方》諸篇，把成王與周公對商遺民發布的文告保存了下來：安撫之語反覆申說商民「非我小國敢弋殷命」，把叛亂定性為少數人的挾眾行為，又以「爾惟舊人，宅乃心」勸商遺民留在舊地、接受周的封受。可見周方在作戰同時展開政治攻心，把殷人從叛軍之中爭取過來，而叛軍最缺乏的正是內部的整合。軍事部署上，後世一直沿用分道並進的說法：東征大軍自周原、關中出發，分成數路，一路壓向殷畿、正面攻武庚，一路直取奄國，另有部隊穩住淮夷與宋地的側面，斷絕叛軍的糧道與外援。文獻與後世注家中常見的「營」「陂」「費」三個地名，一般認為分別指今河南湯陰一帶的營、汜水流域的陂與今山東費縣一帶的費，與由西向東推進的戰線相合，但今地對應仍有爭議。作戰方式上，周人善用車兵與步兵的混合隊形：戰車在前掩護，步兵結陣跟進，弓手在兩翼射擊騷擾；遇到城池則圍而不攻、斷糧待潰，同時以新造的兵車與就地徵集的殷人補充兵力。叛軍則依託商代留下的城邑與封國，據地固守，並靠熟悉的鄉里網絡供應，東線的奄國是最難拔的一處，經長期圍困才被攻破。戰事自公元前1042年起，到公元前1039年前後結束，前後約三年。
tacticsEn: The Duke of Zhou answered this rising first on the political and the logistical plane and only afterwards on the battlefield. The chapters Da Gao, Kang Gao, Jiu Gao, Zi Cai, Duo Shi and Duo Fang of the Shujing preserve the proclamations issued by King Cheng and the Duke to the people of the Shang remnant. Their language of reassurance insists again and again that the people of the Shang were not a small state seeking to seize the Shang mandate, so that the rising was made out as the act of a few men dragging others in; and it urges the old people of the Shang to stay where they were and settle in their hearts, and accept the enfeoffments of the Zhou. The Zhou were therefore carrying on a political offensive at the same time as the fighting, trying to win the Yin people away from the rebels, and what the rebels most lacked was cohesion of their own. As for the military deployment, later generations kept the account of columns advancing by several routes. The eastern expedition left the Zhou plain and the Guanzhong basin and divided: one column pressed on the Yin region and struck at Wu Geng directly, one went for the state of Yan, and other bodies secured the flank towards the Huai and the country of Song, cutting the rebels off from their supplies and from outside help. The three place names that appear in the documents and in later commentary, Ying, Pi and Fei, are generally taken to be Ying near Tangyin in Henan, Pi in the basin of the Si river, and Fei in the county of Fei in Shandong, matching a front moving from west to east, though the identification is still disputed. In method, the Zhou worked with mixed formations of chariots and foot: the chariots led and covered, the infantry closed up behind them in ranks, and archers shot and harassed from the two flanks; when a walled town was met they invested it without storming it and waited for it to starve, at the same time making up the strength with new chariots and with Yin people levied on the spot. The rebels on the other hand held the towns and the client states left over from the Shang, fought from fixed positions, and supplied themselves through the local networks they knew; Yan's resistance on the eastern front was the hardest to break, and the city there fell only after a long investment. The war began in 1042 BC and was over by about 1039 BC, some three years in all.
data: 可核對的數字分三類。第一類是系年與文獻內證：起事繫於公元前1042年，即武王崩後成王即位之年；傳統說法以東征歷時約三年、到公元前1039年前後平定為主流，但《竹書紀年》與《史記·周本紀》的系年互有出入，另有公元前1041、前1040之說。兵員數字在傳世文獻中幾乎全缺，《大誥》只反覆提到「殷民」「商民」被脅迫參戰，說明叛軍的兵力相當程度依賴被強迫的商民，而周軍的規模沒有可考證的數字，只留下「王師」「三軍」這類編制性的稱謂。戰役地名中，營、陂、費三地是後世說法的依據，但今地對應仍有爭議。第二類是考古數字：安陽殷墟自1928年起系統發掘，1936年小屯的YH127窖藏一次出土甲骨約一萬七千片，全墟出土甲骨總數在十五萬片上下，已著錄者約九萬片，可辨甲骨文約四千五百字，卜辭中保存大量征伐與祭祀的記錄；山東萊蕪羊里遺址在1980年代的發掘被學界普遍認定為奄國都城所在，出土帶「奄」與「亞醜」銘文的青銅器，是三監之亂最直接的物質證據；曲阜魯國故城與周公廟一帶1930年代的發掘，顯示戰後此地的周人城邑規劃；陝西岐山周原出土西周甲骨數百片，北京房山琉璃河的燕國遺址也出西周甲骨，都可以與《召誥》所記營造洛邑的年代互相參照。第三類是推估，必須打折：叛軍的實際作戰兵力多在數千人至數萬人量級，絕大多數是被裹挾的殷地民眾；周軍核心則是王師與周原、關中的常備兵力，數量同樣不明。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into three classes. The first is the chronology and the internal evidence of the documents. The rising is dated to 1042 BC, the year after King Wu's death in which King Cheng came to the throne. The usual account is that the eastern campaign lasted about three years and was wound up by about 1039 BC, but the chronologies of the Zhushu Jinian and of the Shiji in the annals of the House of Zhou do not agree exactly, and proposals of 1041 and 1040 BC also exist. Figures for the numbers of troops are almost wholly absent from the transmitted texts: the Da Gao only says again and again that people of Yin and people of Shang were forced to take part, which shows that the rebel strength depended in considerable measure on the coerced people of the Yin country, while the size of the Zhou army leaves no verifiable figure behind and only such formal names as the royal host and the three armies. Among the place names, Ying, Pi and Fei are the basis of the later reconstructions, though their modern identification remains disputed. The second class is archaeological. Yinxu at Anyang has been systematically excavated since 1928; the deposit known as YH127 at Xiaotun yielded on the order of seventeen thousand oracle bones in 1936, and the total from Yinxu stands at around one hundred and fifty thousand pieces, of which roughly ninety thousand have been published, with about four thousand five hundred legible oracle graph characters, the texts preserving a large number of records of campaigns and sacrifices. The site at Yangli in Laiwu, Shandong, excavated in the 1980s, is generally identified by scholars as the capital of the state of Yan, and the bronzes inscribed with the names of Yan and Ya Chou found there are the most direct material evidence for the Sanmon rising. The excavations of the 1930s at the Zhou Gong temple area of the Lu capital at Qufu show the planning of the Zhou settlement on that ground after the war; the Western Zhou oracle bones, several hundred in number, from Zhouyuan at Qishan in Shaanxi, and the Western Zhou oracle bones from the Yan site at Liulihe in Fangshan near Beijing, can both be compared with the dates for the building of Luoyang preserved in the Zao Gao. The third class is estimate and must be discounted. The actual field strength of the rebels is generally put in the range of thousands to tens of thousands, the great majority of them people of the Yin country swept along; the core of the Zhou army was the royal host together with the standing forces of the Zhou plain and of Guanzhong, and its numbers are equally unknown.
cause: 打起來的原因，一半在王室的繼承，一半在新秩序還沒有長出根。第一層是權力交接的真空：武王克商之後兩年而崩，成王年幼，周公以攝政的名義代掌軍國。攝政在禮制上本不是壞事，但缺乏穩定的先例與明確的期限，於是「周公將不利於孺子」的流言在畿內與封國之間迅速傳開，弟弟們的恐懼被寫成了指控。第二層是兄弟之間的具體利益：管、蔡、霍三地是武王分封的諸侯，與周公、康叔的封地犬牙相錯；東征之後殷地要分封一批新的受封者，魯、衛、燕、宋的建立意味著三兄弟的封地與勢力範圍都將被重划，叛亂因此帶有明確的繼承與地盤之爭。第三層是被征服者的回應：武庚作為帝辛之子居於殷，殷民對新王的統治並不服從；《尚書·多方》《多士》所存周人的自白，正說明周人在作戰之餘必須反覆處理商遺民的問題，叛亂給了殷人重整旗鼓的名分。第四層是地理與戰略：東方的奄國是商代大國，商亡後十餘年間一直是周朝的隱患，它加入叛軍使戰線由安陽一帶拉長到曲阜、萊蕪，令周公無法只打一場速決的畿內平叛，必須把戰爭拉長，打成攻守兼備的持久戰。
causeEn: The reasons for the war are half about succession in the royal house and half about the fact that the new order had not yet put down roots. The first layer is the vacuum left by a transfer of power. King Wu died two years after conquering the Shang, King Cheng was a child, and the Duke of Zhou took the army and the government in his own name as regent. Regency was nothing improper in itself under the system of ritual, but it had no settled precedent and no fixed term, and so the rumour that the Duke of Zhou meant harm to the child prince spread quickly through the heartland and the feudal states, with the fear of the younger brothers turned into accusation. The second layer is the concrete interest between brothers. Guan, Cai and Huo were appanages enfeoffed by King Wu and lay interwoven with the lands of the Duke of Zhou and of Kang Shu; after the eastern campaign a new batch of enfeoffments was to be made in the Yin country, and the establishment of Lu, Wei, Yan and Song meant that the appanages and the spheres of influence of the three brothers would all be redrawn, so the rising carried an unmistakable claim to inheritance and to territory. The third layer is the answer of the conquered. Wu Geng, son of Di Xin, sat at Yin, and the people of Yin did not accept the rule of the new king; the confessions of the Zhou preserved in the Duo Fang and the Duo Shi show that even while they fought they had to keep dealing with the question of the Shang remnant, and the rising gave the Yin people a name under which to raise their heads again. The fourth layer is geography and strategy. The state of Yan in the east had been a great power under the Shang and remained a latent trouble for the Zhou for more than a decade after the fall of the Shang; its entry into the rising stretched the front from the neighbourhood of Anyang to Qufu and Laiwu, and left the Duke of Zhou unable to fight a quick decision in the heartland alone. The war had to be prolonged into a struggle of attack and defence in which both sides held.
impact: 三監之亂平定之後，西周的局面才真正穩定下來，這場戰爭的歷史重量遠超過它本身的規模。第一，它結束了商周交替的最後一個變數：武庚死、奄國滅，殷地與東方的反抗被壓下去，周人此後不必再面對一位被承認的商王繼承人。第二，它催生了西周最重要的兩項制度工程：封建與定都。齊、魯、衛、燕、宋一批諸侯在戰後受封，構成西周前半葉的統治骨架；而洛陽的成周從此成為周王的東都與東方諸侯的總指揮部，《召誥》記周公「攻位」、《洛誥》記周公「宅」於洛邑，周公還政之後成王親理政事，於是形成天子與諸侯的雙層秩序。第三，它讓禮樂制度的推行成為可能：管蔡霍之亂本會讓天下人懷疑周的德行，周公用三年征討、數年教化之後歸政，這段攝政與還政的故事，後來被儒家援引為周公製禮作樂的樣板，也成了後世論證權力可以和平歸還的經典範例。第四，它在考古上極為重要：萊蕪羊里、安陽殷墟、曲阜魯故城、岐山周原、房山琉璃河等遺址，串出西周初年東方諸侯國的地理框架；甲骨學的興起也與此直接相關——1899年王懿榮在安陽發現甲骨文字，劉鶚的《鐵雲藏龜》於1903年問世，王國維在1917年以二重證據法證成《史記》所記商王世系與甲骨文相合，自此西周紀年才有一個可以檢驗的骨架。
impactEn: It was only after the Sanmon rising had been put down that the Western Zhou order really settled, and the historical weight of this war is far greater than its scale. First, it closed the last variable in the passage from the Shang to the Zhou. Wu Geng was dead, the state of Yan was destroyed, the resistance of the Yin country and of the east was suppressed, and the Zhou never again had to face a Shang successor whose claim was recognised. Second, it brought into being the two institutional works that mattered most in the early Western Zhou: enfeoffment and a fixed capital. A batch of lords, of Qi, Lu, Wei, Yan and Song, were enfeoffed after the war and formed the skeleton of rule in the first half of the dynasty; and the completed Zhou at Luoyang became the eastern capital of the king and the headquarters for the eastern lords. The Zao Gao records the Duke of Zhou fixing the site, the Luo Gao records him making his dwelling at Luoyang, and after the Duke returned the government King Cheng took charge of affairs himself, so that a two-tier order of king and lords was formed. Third, it made the enforcement of the system of rites and music possible. The revolt of Guan, Cai and Huo might have left all under heaven doubting the virtue of the Zhou; the Duke ended it with three years of campaigning and several years of instruction before giving power back, and this story of regency and return became the model later Confucians used for the Duke of Zhou making the rites and the music, and the classic example by which later ages argued that power may be handed back in peace. Fourth, it matters enormously for archaeology. The sites at Yangli in Laiwu, Yinxu at Anyang, the Lu capital at Qufu, Zhouyuan at Qishan and Liulihe in Fangshan together lay out the geographical framework of the eastern states of the early Western Zhou; and the rise of oracle-bone studies is directly connected with it. In 1899 Wang Yirong found oracle-bone writing at Anyang; Liu E published the Tieyun Canggui in 1903; and in 1917 Wang Guowei used the method of double evidence to show that the lineage of Shang kings recorded in the Shiji matched the oracle bones, and only then did the chronology of the early Western Zhou acquire a frame that could be checked.
result: 公元前1042年成王即位之年，叛亂在殷畿與奄國兩處同時爆開，周公旦自領王師東征，前後約三年，到公元前1039年前後大致了結。戰果記載相當簡略：武庚伏誅，管叔被殺；蔡叔與霍叔一度出奔，後被貶為庶人，而管、蔡、霍三族的封地被收回，周人以新受封的康叔度出封衛、召公奭封燕、周公封魯、微子封宋，補上關鍵的幾個位置。奄國的抵抗最為頑強，傳世文獻說周公「居東二年，則罪人斯得」，也說東征前後歷三年，萊蕪一帶的城邑最終被攻破，奄的族眾或被遷徙、或被併入魯地。戰後的收束才是真正的收束：周公營建洛邑成周，把殷人一批一批安置到新都與舊地，周公歸政於成王，成王親政，王室的典章、祭祀與刑罰從此有了固定的格式。結果可以這樣概括：三監之亂以流血的平叛收場，卻贏得了兩樣東西——殷地與東方的安寧，以及一套可以傳世的周家秩序；而它留下的教訓同樣清楚：王室內部的裂痕若在最脆弱的時刻爆發，勝方靠的不只是兵力，更是《尚書》諸篇所顯示的那套把政令、撫恤與祭祀結合起來的手段。
resultEn: In the year 1042 BC, the year of King Cheng's accession, the rising broke out at once in the Yin region and in the state of Yan, and the Duke of Zhou, Dan, took the royal host east himself. It lasted about three years and was wound up by roughly 1039 BC. The record of the results is very brief. Wu Geng was executed and Guan Shu was killed; Cai Shu and Huo Shu fled for a time and were afterwards reduced to commoners, while the three fiefs of Guan, Cai and Huo were taken back, and the Zhou filled the most important of the vacant places with new enfeoffments: Kang Shu Du in Wei, Shao Gong Shi in Yan, the Duke of Zhou himself in Lu and Weizi in Song. The resistance of Yan was the most stubborn; the transmitted texts say that the Duke of Zhou stayed in the east two years and then the guilty were taken, and that the eastern campaign ran for three years, and the towns in the Laiwu country were broken at last, the people of Yan being moved away or absorbed into the lands of Lu. The tidying up after the war was the real conclusion. The Duke of Zhou built the completed Zhou at Luoyang, moved the people of Yin by instalments into the new capital and into their old country, the Duke returned the government to King Cheng, King Cheng took charge in person, and from then on the ceremonies, the sacrifices and the penal law of the royal house had a fixed form. The result can be put in this way. The Sanmon rising ended in a blood-soaked suppression, but it won two things: the peace of the Yin country and of the east, and a Zhou order that could be handed down. The lesson it leaves is just as plain. When the cracks inside a royal house break open at the moment of greatest weakness, what carries the winning side is not only the weight of arms, but the combination of government orders, care for the people and sacrifice that the chapters of the Shujing display.
